# How to use Markdown Preview

Markdown Preview is a browser-based editor: type or open Markdown on the left, and see a live preview on the right. Everything runs locally in your browser.

This guide covers how to use the app and every Markdown feature it supports.

---

## Getting started

1. Open the app in your browser (or install it as a Progressive Web App).
2. Type Markdown in the editor, or load a file (see [Opening files](#opening-files)).
3. Watch the preview update as you type.
4. Use the toolbar for themes, export, share links, present mode, and more.

### Opening files

- **Upload** — Use the upload button to open `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.html`, or `.htm` files.
- **Drag and drop** — Drop a file onto the window to load it.
- **Open with (PWA)** — An installed app can register as a handler for `.md` / `.markdown` files.

When Markdown arrives from a share link, upload, or OS file open, an **External content** dialog asks you to **Accept** or **Reject** it.

### Paste an image

Copy an image (screenshot, browser copy, or file from an image editor), focus the Markdown editor, and paste (`Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`V`).

The app inserts a Markdown image at the caret using a base64 data URI:

```markdown
![image](data:image/png;base64,)
```

That example renders as:

![image](data:image/png;base64,)

Notes:

- Max size is **2 MB**. Larger pastes are rejected with a toast.
- If you have text selected when you paste, that selection becomes the image alt text.
- In the editor, long `data:` URIs collapse to a short chip so the source stays readable; the full URI is used for preview and export.
- You can still write normal URL images: `![Alt text](https://example.com/photo.png)`.

### Files drawer

Available on Chromium desktop when the File System Access API is supported. Open it with the hamburger button.

| Action | What it does |
|--------|----------------|
| **Open folder** | Pick a local folder to browse (handle remembered for next visits) |
| **New** | Create a new untitled document |
| **New folder** | Create a subfolder in the current directory |
| **Refresh** | Reload the folder tree |
| **Save** / `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`S` | Write the current file when a handle is available |
| **Outline** | Heading list for the open document; click to jump in editor and preview |

Right-click (or long-press) a file or folder for a context menu: **New file**, **New folder**, **Rename**, **Delete**.

If permission to the saved folder was revoked, the drawer shows **Allow access** or **Choose folder** so you can re-grant it.

### Editor and preview layout

- The Markdown **editor** is syntax-highlighted (see [Editor highlighting](#editor-highlighting)).
- Drag the **splitter** between panes (or focus it and use arrow keys) to resize. `Home` / `End` snap to the extremes.
- Collapse the editor or preview with the pane buttons for more space.
- Optional **sync scroll** keeps editor and preview scroll positions aligned.
- Choose **Readable** or **Full** preview width from the toolbar.

### Editor highlighting

The editor overlays a highlighted view of your Markdown source (same highlighting engine as code blocks in the preview).

- Highlighting is active for documents under about **100 KB**.
- Larger files keep a plain textarea so typing stays fast.
- Fenced code blocks in the **preview** are highlighted separately, with line numbers when a language is recognized.

### Themes

Pick a theme from the dropdown. Your choice is remembered:

| Theme | Look |
|-------|------|
| GitHub Light | Default light |
| GitHub Dark | Default dark |
| Sepia | Warm parchment, serif |
| Terminal | Green on black, monospace |
| Salesforce Cosmos | SLDS-inspired palette |
| Fancy | Decorative headings and background photo |

### Views

| Mode | What it does |
|------|----------------|
| **Edit** | Split editor + live preview (default) |
| **Reader** | Preview only — good for reading shared links |
| **Present** | Full-screen walk through `h1` / `h2` sections |
| **Slides** | Same section walk, but the editor stays open |

**Present / Slides navigation:** `←` `→` `↑` `↓`, `Space`, `PageUp` / `PageDown`, `Home` / `End`, or swipe. Exit with **Exit** or `Escape`.

### Draft auto-save and local history

Your current draft is **auto-saved** to `localStorage` as you type, so reloading the page restores your work.

Separately, **History** keeps up to **20** recent snapshots (also in `localStorage`, capped around 200 000 characters total). Snapshots are written after a short idle pause. Open the history dropdown in the toolbar to restore an earlier version.

> [!TIP]
> Auto-save keeps the latest draft. History lets you step back if you overwrite something you still need.

### Print

Use the toolbar **Print** button to print the current preview (or choose “Save as PDF” in the system print dialog). Print styles hide the chrome and keep the article clean.

This is separate from **Export → PDF**, which builds a dedicated print document in a hidden frame (better for Mermaid diagrams and a clean export filename).

### Export

From **Export**, choose:

| Format | Notes |
|--------|--------|
| **HTML** | Self-contained document with styles |
| **PDF** | Browser print engine via a hidden frame (“Save as PDF”) |
| **Markdown** | Source plus YAML front matter (`title`, `generator`) |
| **DOCX** | Basic Word document (images become `[Image: alt]` placeholders) |
| **RTF** | Rich Text Format export |

### Share links

**Copy reader link** or **Copy present link** compresses your Markdown into a URL (`#mdz=…` with theme and view). Long documents may produce links that are too large for some browsers; a toast warns when that happens.

### Read aloud and voice picker

Use the **Read aloud** control to hear the preview. In supported browsers, words are highlighted as they are spoken.

- **Play / Stop** — start or stop reading.
- **Pause / Resume** — pause mid-document and continue.
- **Voice picker** (chevron next to the speak control) — choose among high-quality English voices. Your choice is remembered. Prefer Neural / cloud voices when available for clearer speech.

The speak controls are hidden if the browser has no speech synthesis support.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Context | Action |
|----------|---------|--------|
| `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`S` | Edit view, file open | Save current file |
| `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`V` | Editor focused, image on clipboard | Paste image as Markdown |
| `→` `↓` `Space` `PageDown` | Present / Slides | Next section |
| `←` `↑` `PageUp` | Present / Slides | Previous section |
| `Home` | Present / Slides | First section |
| `End` | Present / Slides | Last section |
| `Escape` | Present / Slides or open menus | Exit present / close menus |
| `←` `→` `↑` `↓` | Splitter focused | Resize panes |
| `Home` / `End` | Splitter focused | Snap splitter to extremes |

### Install / offline

Install as a PWA when the browser offers it. After install, the app and its libraries work offline. When an update is waiting, a banner asks you to reload.

---

## Supported Markdown

The preview uses **GitHub Flavored Markdown** (GFM), plus Mermaid diagrams, GitHub alert callouts, emoji shortcodes / emoticons, and YAML front matter as a metadata table.

> [!NOTE]
> Soft line breaks are off: a single newline does **not** become a `<br>`. End a line with two spaces for a hard break, or use a blank line for a new paragraph.

### Headings

```markdown
# Heading 1
## Heading 2
### Heading 3
#### Heading 4
##### Heading 5
###### Heading 6
```

Setext-style headings also work:

```markdown
Heading 1
=========

Heading 2
---------
```

`h1` and `h2` headings define sections for Present and Slides mode.

### Emphasis

```markdown
*italic* or _italic_
**bold** or __bold__
***bold italic***
~~strikethrough~~
```

### Paragraphs and line breaks

Separate paragraphs with a blank line.

For a hard line break inside a paragraph, end the line with two spaces:

```markdown
Line one␠␠
Line two
```

### Links and images

```markdown
[Link text](https://example.com)
[Link with title](https://example.com "Title")

![Alt text](https://example.com/image.png)
![Alt](https://example.com/image.png "Title")
```

To embed from the clipboard, see [Paste an image](#paste-an-image).

Reference-style links:

```markdown
[Example][id]

[id]: https://example.com "Optional title"
```

Autolinks (GFM):

```markdown
<https://example.com>
https://example.com
```

### Lists

Unordered:

```markdown
- Item
* Item
+ Item
  - Nested item
```

Ordered:

```markdown
1. First
2. Second
   1. Nested
```

Task lists:

```markdown
- [ ] Unchecked task
- [x] Checked task
```

### Blockquotes

```markdown
> A quoted paragraph.
>
> > Nested quote
```

### Horizontal rules

```markdown
---
***
___
```

### Code

Inline code:

```markdown
Use `code` in a sentence.
```

Fenced code blocks (language for syntax highlighting):

````markdown
```javascript
function hello() {
  return "world";
}
```
````

Tilde fences and indented code blocks (4 spaces or a tab) are also supported. Preview code blocks get line numbers and highlighting when the language is recognized.

### Tables

```markdown
| Left | Center | Right |
|:-----|:------:|------:|
| a    | b      | c     |
| d    | e      | f     |
```

Pipes inside inline code in a table cell stay in that cell, for example `` `|` `` does not split the column.

### Inline HTML

Raw HTML is allowed and then sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and similar are stripped). Prefer Markdown when possible.

### Escaping

Backslash-escape special characters when you need the literal character:

```markdown
\*not italic\*
\[not a link\]
```

---

## Mermaid diagrams

Use a fenced block with the language `mermaid`. Diagrams render as SVG in the preview (and in HTML / PDF export).

Source:

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
  A[Start] --> B{OK?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Done]
  B -->|No| A
```
````

Rendered example:

```mermaid
graph TD
  A[Start] --> B{OK?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Done]
  B -->|No| A
```

Common diagram types include flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, entity-relationship diagrams, Gantt charts, pie charts, git graphs, mindmaps, and timelines — anything Mermaid itself supports.

---

## YAML front matter

A YAML block at the very start of the document (between `---` lines) is shown as a key–value metadata table at the top of the preview. Nested values (lists, maps) appear as readable YAML in the value cell. Mid-document `---` rules are unchanged.

Docs-oriented fields such as `intro`, `permissions`, or `versions` are shown as data only — they are not turned into page layout chrome.

```markdown
---
title: About your personal dashboard
versions:
  fpt: '*'
  ghes: '>=3.11'
---

# Heading

Body content…
```

If the YAML is invalid, the block is still consumed (so it does not become horizontal rules) and the preview shows an “Invalid YAML” note with the raw text.

---

## GitHub alert callouts

Start a blockquote with `[!TYPE]`. Types are case-insensitive.

> [!NOTE]
> Useful information readers should know.

> [!TIP]
> Optional advice that helps someone succeed.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Crucial information for success.

> [!WARNING]
> Critical content that needs attention.

> [!CAUTION]
> Negative consequences of an action.

Source form:

```markdown
> [!NOTE]
> Useful information readers should know.

> [!TIP]
> Optional advice that helps someone succeed.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Crucial information for success.

> [!WARNING]
> Critical content that needs attention.

> [!CAUTION]
> Negative consequences of an action.
```

---

## Emoji

### Shortcodes

Any [gemoji](https://github.com/github/gemoji) short name works:

```markdown
:wink: :heart: :rocket: :tada: :+1: :warning:
```

Renders as: :wink: :heart: :rocket: :tada: :+1: :warning:

### Emoticons

Common ASCII faces convert to emoji (skipped inside URLs so `http://` is safe):

| Type this | Get |
|-----------|-----|
| `:-)` `:)` `=)` `=]` | 🙂 |
| `:-D` `:D` `=D` | 😀 |
| `;-)` `;)` | 😉 |
| `:-(` `:(` | 😦 |
| `:'(` | 😢 |
| `:')` and related joy faces | 😂 |
| `<3` | ❤️ |
| `</3` | 💔 |
| `:-P` `:P` | 😛 |
| `8-)` `8)` | 😎 |
| `>:(` | 😠 |
| `o:-)` `O:)` | 😇 |
| `:/` `:-/` | 😕 |
| `:*` `:-*` | 😘 |
| `:|` `:-|` | 😐 |
| `:o` `:O` | 😮 |
| `:@` | 😡 |

## Quick reference

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Headings `#` … `######`, Setext | Yes |
| Bold, italic, strikethrough | Yes |
| Links, images, paste image (data URI) | Yes |
| Lists, nested lists, task lists | Yes |
| Tables (including `` `|` `` in cells) | Yes |
| Fenced / indented code + highlighting | Yes |
| Blockquotes | Yes |
| Mermaid diagrams | Yes |
| GitHub alerts (`NOTE`, `TIP`, …) | Yes |
| YAML front matter (metadata table) | Yes |
| Emoji shortcodes and emoticons | Yes |
| Inline HTML (sanitized) | Yes |
| Soft breaks (single newline → `<br>`) | No — use two trailing spaces |
| Math / LaTeX | No |
| Footnotes | No |
| Definition lists | No |

---

## Tips

- Structure long documents with `#` and `##` so Present and Slides mode feel natural.
- Prefer share **reader** links for reading and **present** links for walkthroughs.
- Mermaid and syntax highlighting work best in the live preview and in HTML / PDF export; DOCX / RTF are simpler text-oriented exports.
- Use **Print** for a quick hard copy; use **Export → PDF** when you want a cleaner Mermaid-friendly save.
- Install the PWA if you want offline editing and “Open with” for Markdown files.
